title: Spectral Sidon Sets in Matrix Algebras: Non-Commutative Packing Advantages, Hierarchical Hessenberg Decoding, and Arithmetic Obstructions
abstract: We initiate the study of Spectral Sidon Sets in matrix algebras: subsets A of M_d(R) whose pairwise sums A + B all have distinct characteristic polynomials det(tI - (A + B)). While d = 1 recovers classical Sidon sets, d >= 2 exposes a deep interplay between non-commutativity, matrix invariant theory, algebraic number theory, and analytic number theory. We prove six foundational results: (1) a Universal Commuting Ceiling showing via Wedderburn-Artin decomposition and discriminant-free Minkowski l_infty-ball packing that every commuting subset of M_d([0,N]) -- even non-symmetric and arbitrarily nilpotent -- has size at most sqrt(2)*(4dN+1)^(d/2) = O_d(N^(d/2)); (2) exact asymptotic determination sigma_d(N) = Theta_d(N^(d(d+1)/4)) for all d >= 2 via a new Hierarchical Hessenberg Spectral Decoding Theorem, recovering all d(d+1)/2 full-scale entries of an upper-Hessenberg matrix from its characteristic polynomial alone and beating every commuting family by N^(d(d-1)/4); (3) a strict symmetric-vs-non-symmetric arithmetic separation at d = 2 via Landau sum-of-two-squares theorem (sigma_2^sym(N) <= (sqrt(30*sqrt(2)*K_LR)+o(1)) N^(3/2)/(log N)^(1/4) = o(sigma_2(N))) alongside an intermediate Erdos-Ford multiplication-table barrier in the equal-diagonal hyperbolic subspace; (4) a symmetric Jacobi-band breakthrough sigma_d^sym(N) = Omega_d(N^((3d-1)/4)) for all d >= 2, an exact parity rectangular injectivity threshold at u <= sqrt(N) saturated by explicit integer symmetric collisions at u = sqrt(N)+O(1), and spectral additive energy Omega(N^9 sqrt(log N)) <= E_spec(Sym_2([0,N])) <= O(N^9 log N) showing uniform probabilistic alteration stalls at Omega(N/(log N)^(1/3)); (5) characteristic-2 collapse, an exact d = 2 finite-field commuting ceiling |A| <= q matched by Omega(q) for p >= 5, and machine-checked non-commutative witnesses breaking commuting ceilings in Sym_2(F_5, F_7, F_11, F_13) and Sym_3(F_3, F_5); and (6) a super-exponential Galois-torus separation showing the elliptic torus F_{p^d} -> M_d(F_p) beats every split-diagonal family for all even d >= 8 and all d >= 25 (including all odd d >= 25). The algebraic and finite-field core (16 constructive theorems) is formalized in Lean 4.36.0 (0 sorry, 0 grind, 0 custom axioms).
